text:
alex: Proposal: phasewise hydration for very large bundles (>1T). aim is to lower startup memory and make warmup predictable. rough manifest addition: hydration_policy + phases array.

maria: sounds promising. how do we handle compatibility with existing index-first loaders? also curious about canary/rollout safety.

sam.b: main worry is tail latency for cold layers. recommend pairing with a deterministic fallback model (e.g., quant-7B) and a metric for fallback_rate.

kai: prefer minimal manifest changes. suggest an API primitive ensure_phase(name, strategy, timeout_ms) so loaders can be policy-driven rather than heuristic.

lina: observability reqs: per-phase latency histograms, hydration_fallback_rate metric, and trace spans named like hydrate:phase:<name>. alert if fallback rate >0.5% over 5m.

alex: API sketch: ensure_phase("layers-0-31", strategy="block|async_prefetch|background", timeout_ms=2000). manifest example (in thread but not a field) with phases: meta, kvcache, layers-0-31, layers-32-63 and prefetch_hints for prefixes.

maria: streaming partial responses for cold layers worries me; better to return a short apology + fallback then retry once hydrated. avoids gibberish.

sam.b: agree. fallback mapping contract: small_model pinned as bundle_id:compat:<level>, runtime exposes percent_of_requests_fallback.

warmup-bot: perf-sim (bundle=gptx-1.5t-v2, policy=conservative) results: median cold-start +26ms, 95p +340ms, memory peak -11%. report: https://ci.example/reports/3687654321

lina: numbers look good. i'll make dashboards for per-phase latency and fallback correlation.
kai: migration note: add manifest_version and phase_uuid so loaders detect changed phase boundaries and fail fast.
alex: i'll produce a test bundle and traces. sam.b please create staging ticket to land ensure_phase and fallback path.
sam.b: creating ticket now and will add PoC wiring to staging canary with quant-7B fallback.
alex: thanks all, will follow up with manifest patch and perf sims. :thumbsup:
